tags.name: SESSION_OPEN_REQUESTED
tags.note: SessionController.openSession() entry. Driver is the selected model name; workspace and bundle are nullable if the caller left them unset.

tags.name: SESSION_OPEN_ACKED
tags.note: The server returned a session_id on POST /api/session. name is nullable when the server has not yet named the record.

tags.name: SESSION_OPEN_REFUSED
tags.note: POST /api/session failed. failure_class is the typed reason from the SubstrateClient; detail is a human string.

field_types.failure_class: string (client failure class: network, http_error, or the server's failure_class)
field_types.detail: string (server error text; Layer 7 bounds it)

tags.name: SESSION_ATTACH_STARTED
tags.note: attachExisting(sessionId) began; the controller is opening the SSE stream against a session it did not itself create.

tags.name: SESSION_END_REQUESTED
tags.note: endSession(reason) entry. reason is the caller's label: user_end (the end-session confirm, /exit) or user_close (Close Pane, ⌘W).

tags.name: SESSION_ENDED_LOCAL
tags.note: A SessionEnded envelope reached the controller; snapshot flipped to endedReason. Distinct from SESSION_END_REQUESTED because a session can end without the local caller asking.

tags.name: DRIVER_ROSTER_LOADED
tags.note: loadDriverRoster() populated snapshot.driverRoster from /api/models. default is nullable when the server names no default.

tags.name: DRIVER_PICKED
tags.note: pickDriver(name) was called. The controller records the choice; no server call fires until session-open.

tags.name: DRIVER_VERSION_PICKED
tags.note: pickDriverVersion(driver, versionId) was called. version is null when the pick is cleared and the server will fall back to the CLI's default_version. Only meaningful for CLI drivers; ollama tags carry their model in the driver name.

tags.name: BUNDLE_ROSTER_LOADED
tags.note: loadBundleRoster() populated snapshot.bundleRoster from /api/bundles.

tags.name: BUNDLE_PICKED
tags.note: pickBundle(slug) was called. Records the choice; no server call fires until session-open.

tags.name: WORKSPACES_LOADED
tags.note: loadRecentWorkspaces() populated snapshot.recentWorkspaces from /api/workspaces.

tags.name: TURN_SUBMITTED
tags.note: sendTurn(text) entry. turn_index counts from zero over the session's lifetime; text_length is the trimmed input character count. v0.49: attachments, the chips sent with it. v0.50: saved, the buffers saved for the turn before it was posted (0 when there were none; EDITOR_SAVED_FOR_SEND).

field_types.attachments: int (the chips sent with the message; D94)
field_types.saved: int (buffers of the session saved before the turn; SAVE-BEFORE-SEND-2026-11-10)

tags.name: TURN_ACK
tags.note: POST /api/session/<id>/turn returned 200. The envelope stream carries the model's reply from here on.

tags.name: TURN_REFUSED
tags.note: Turn POST failed. failure_class is the typed reason; detail is the human string.

field_types.failure_class: string (client failure class: network, http_error, or the server's failure_class)
field_types.detail: string (server error text; Layer 7 bounds it)

tags.name: TURN_PARKED
tags.note: A Park envelope arrived; the driver is waiting on the human. park_reason names the wait (rate_limit, awaiting_input, etc).

tags.name: TURN_INTERRUPTED
tags.note: interruptTurn() completed. was_interrupted true when the server killed an in-flight turn; landed is the server's ACK for the interrupt; tier is soft or hard; signal true for Ctrl+C, false for /interrupt; scope names what got interrupted.

tags.name: STREAM_ATTACHED
tags.note: SSE onopen; snapshot.connection = 'connected'. Payload carries session_id for a session stream, record_root for a child-record attach. Exactly one of the two is present.

tags.name: STREAM_CLOSED
tags.note: SSE closed cleanly (RunFinalised, session-end, or attach to a new session). Same session_id/record_root branching as STREAM_ATTACHED.

tags.name: STREAM_RECONNECTING
tags.note: SSE error tripped the 1s reconnect timer. Same session_id/record_root branching as STREAM_ATTACHED.

tags.name: STREAM_ENVELOPE_APPENDED
tags.note: One envelope folded into the transcript. seq is the substrate Run's monotonic sequence number; kind is the envelope kind string (UserMessage, ModelReply, ToolCall, etc).

tags.name: SESSIONS_LOADED
tags.note: loadLiveSessions() populated snapshot.liveSessions from /api/session.

tags.name: CHILD_RECORD_ATTACH_REQUESTED
tags.note: attachRecordRoot(recordRoot) entry. The controller is subscribing to a child record's stream (a delegate tool call's substrate Run).

tags.name: TOPOLOGY_LOADED
tags.note: loadTopologyGraph(name) returned. Counts describe the structure of the record's authored topology.

tags.name: SPEC_VALIDATE_REQUESTED
tags.note: validateSpec() entry. topology_name is present when the spec names one.

tags.name: SPEC_VALIDATED
tags.note: Server responded to /api/validate. valid is the boolean verdict; error carries the reason on false.

tags.name: SPEC_BUILD_REQUESTED
tags.note: buildSpec() entry. topology_name is present when the spec names one.

tags.name: SPEC_BUILD_REJECTED
tags.note: The server refused the build, or the validator rejected the spec before POST.

tags.name: SPEC_BUILT
tags.note: The build succeeded and a substrate Run was started. run_name is the record identifier; status is the Run's terminal or in-flight state; unfired_triggers_count is present when at least one trigger in the authored topology never fired.

field_types.status: string (the run's state as /api/build returns it, or unknown)

tags.name: SLASH_ROUTED
tags.note: submitLine() matched a known slash. cmd is the leading token (exit, model, help, clear, interrupt, name, list, tools, workspace, bundle, isolate).

tags.name: SLASH_UNKNOWN
tags.note: submitLine() matched no known slash. cmd is the leading token.

tags.name: RUN_STARTED
tags.note: A TopologyRunStarted reached this session's record. sessions lists the run's sessions (session_id, role, record_root, driven); t is the record's write time, which the shell reads to open panes only for a run that starts now.

tags.name: RUN_FOCUS_REQUESTED
tags.note: `/run focus` named a run; the shell focuses its pane, or opens one.

field_types.sessions: list of {session_id, role, record_root, driven} (the run's sessions, as RUN_STARTED)

tags.name: RUN_STOP_REQUESTED
tags.note: The server accepted a stop for one of this session's runs; the run's session ends caller_stop.

tags.name: TURN_REFUSED_VIEW_ONLY
tags.note: A line was sent in a pane that shows a run's session, whose topology writes its messages; nothing was posted.

tags.name: DELEGATE_CHILD_STARTED
tags.note: A delegate call this session made now started a child session (its parent is this session); the shell opens an interactive pane on it.

tags.name: ASSAYS_LOADED
tags.note: loadAssays() read /api/assays: one row per cells file in the bench results folder. count is the number of rows.

tags.name: ASSAY_REPORT_LOADED
tags.note: loadAssayReport(name) read /api/assay/<name>: one assay's arm matrix. arms is the number of arms in the report.

tags.name: PICKER_FOLDER_ARMED
tags.note: A pane's picker armed a folder and moved to the model column. source: row (a listed folder or the sandbox row), dialog (choose folder), typed (the path box).
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx (armWorkspace, disarmWorkspace, enterGuidance, pickGuidance, pickLength, commitPane, wsKey)

tags.name: PICKER_FOLDER_DISARMED
tags.note: A pane's picker dropped its armed folder and went back to the folder column. cause: escape, arrow_left, list_click (a click on the folder list's empty space), typed (the path box changed).
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx (armWorkspace, disarmWorkspace, enterGuidance, pickGuidance, pickLength, commitPane, wsKey)

tags.name: PICKER_LINE_ENTERED
tags.note: A pane's picker moved to a line: model, guidance, length or tone. cause: picked (the line before it was picked) or back (escape or arrow up from the line after it).
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx (armWorkspace, disarmWorkspace, enterGuidance, pickGuidance, pickLength, commitPane, wsKey)

tags.name: PICKER_COMMITTED
tags.note: The tone pick bound the pane to its folder; the chat prompt shows and the session opens on the first message.
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx (armWorkspace, disarmWorkspace, enterGuidance, pickGuidance, pickLength, commitPane, wsKey)

tags.name: APP_BOOTED
tags.note: First signal of an app launch: which build and vocabulary is running and which store it uses. Opens the AppBoot session; every other tag of the launch carries its boot_id. v0.53: gate_isolated, true when a gate launched the app with SUBSTRATE_GATE_ISOLATE=1: its windows take no focus and let the OS's mouse through, so a person working on the machine cannot reach them.

tags.name: APP_QUIT_REQUESTED
tags.note: Quit began. cause: app (a quit asked of the app from outside main's code: Cmd-Q, the Dock, logout or a test driver; Electron does not say which), last_window (the last window closed, off macOS), startup_failed (the backend did not come up), backend_died (the backend stopped while the app ran; the user chose Relaunch or Quit).

tags.name: APP_QUIT_COMPLETED
tags.note: The launch ended; the server's exit and the trace's write and loss counts. Closes the AppBoot session.

tags.name: SERVER_SPAWNED
tags.note: Main started the server process.

tags.name: SERVER_BOUND
tags.note: The server reported its port; ms since spawn.

tags.name: SERVER_EXITED
tags.note: The server process ended. An incident when expected is false: the window has no backend. error_type names the exception the server died of, read from its stderr, when it printed a traceback (a crash before its own trace opened leaves no other record).

field_types.error_type: string (the exception class on the last line of the server's stderr traceback, when it printed one)

tags.name: WINDOW_OPENED
tags.note: Main created a window. cause: boot (the first window), menu (File ▸ New Window), activate (the Dock with no window open). A second instance or a deep link focuses the current window and opens none.

tags.name: WINDOW_CLOSED
tags.note: A window closed.

tags.name: NAVIGATION_BLOCKED
tags.note: The window tried to leave the app's page and main refused it.

tags.name: DEEP_LINK_RECEIVED
tags.note: The OS passed a substrate:// link.

tags.name: MENU_COMMAND_SENT
tags.note: A native menu item fired and main sent its command to the window.

tags.name: NATIVE_DIALOG_CLOSED
tags.note: A native file dialog closed. dialog: pick_folder, open_record. outcome: picked, cancelled.

tags.name: WINDOW_BOOTED
tags.note: The window's page started its boot, before the pane registry is built, so it is the window's first record (S1). Opens the Window session in the window's own trace.

tags.name: VIEW_CHANGED
tags.note: The window's open view changed: panes, meta, editor (the code editor view, ⌘⇧E, on the focused pane's session; v0.29) or a page. cause: key, button, menu, split, records_open, close; language when the /language command opens meta on the language lens; tweak when the design tool's view prop sets it.

field_types.cause: enum key | button | menu | split | records_open | close | language | tweak

tags.name: KEY_ROUTED
tags.note: A named key (never a typed character) was routed. action: the keymap action or none; target: picker, records, language, window, box. v0.58: an ⌥ chord that acts is named by its physical letter (Alt+A), since macOS gives the key the composed character (å).

field_types.key: string (named key with modifiers, e.g. Enter, Escape, Meta+d; never a printable character)
field_types.target: enum picker | records | language | window | box | editor | none

tags.name: UNDO_ROUTED
tags.note: Edit ▸ Undo or Redo (⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z; the menu owns them and the window routes them, roadmap r8 key table) went where the undo boundary sends it (BLACKBOARD 2026-11-09): buffer — the editor's buffer undo while it has unsaved changes (redo while its redo stack has steps); history — HISTORY's step back or forward; page — outside the editor, the focused text box's own undo; none — nothing to undo there. Never names the text undone.

tags.name: DIALOG_OPENED
tags.note: The window opened one of its dialogs.

tags.name: CONTEXT_MENU_OPENED
tags.note: The window's right-click menu drawn (D94: right-click › Add to message; BLACKBOARD 2026-11-11, drawn in the page). source: where the right-click was: a row of the editor's files tree, an editor tab, a row of the editor's search results, or the editor's code. items: the items drawn. No label or path (E1).

tags.name: CONTEXT_MENU_CLOSED
tags.note: The right-click menu closed: an item picked (↵ or a click), Escape (the key map's close cascade, ahead of the interrupt), a press outside it, or the window losing focus. Follows its CONTEXT_MENU_OPENED; a menu opened over an open one closes that one outside first.

tags.name: DIALOG_CLOSED
tags.note: A window dialog closed. outcome: confirmed, cancelled, escape.

tags.name: PANE_OPENED
tags.note: A pane was created. cause: start (a pane the window starts with: pane 1, or the layout's tweak props), split (the user split a pane), run (a run's session opened beside its caller), delegate (a delegate child opened beside its caller).
tags.emit_site: web/reveal.ts (pane 1, where its controller is spawned); web/app/App.tsx componentDidMount (the other starting panes), componentDidUpdate (the commit that shows the change)

tags.name: PANE_CLOSED
tags.note: A pane was removed. had_session: it showed a session or record, not its picker.
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate (the commit that shows the change)

tags.name: PANE_FOCUSED
tags.note: Focus moved to a pane. cause: click (the user clicked it), split (the pane just made by a split), open (a run or delegate pane already showing, or its caller before the split beside it), close (the neighbour of the pane just closed).
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate (the commit that shows the change)

tags.name: PANE_BOUND
tags.note: A pane stopped showing its picker: the window marked it bound, or its controller holds a session. binding: session or record (a run's record). how: picker (the picker committed), attach (a session picked under a workspace row or on the records page), run, child (a delegate child), restore (the ?session= of a reload), direct (the controller opened or attached a session through window.__vm, outside the window's controls: the gates' driver and the registry's calls). session_id when the window knows it at that commit.
tags.emit_site: web/app/App.tsx componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate (the commit that shows the change)

field_types.how: enum picker | attach | run | child | restore | direct

tags.name: LENS_CHANGED
tags.note: Meta's lens changed: stream (drawn with its graph, the chip reads stream+graph), structure, language, scene, io. Written when the lens differs from the one shown.

field_types.lens: enum stream | structure | language | scene | io

tags.name: TRANSCRIPT_ROW_DRAWN
tags.note: A record entry of a session became a row on screen. The view pair of every kernel session kind the window shows (kernel session vocabulary § G).

field_types.session_id: string or null (the kernel session id; null in a pane showing an attached record, whose RECORD_OPENED names it)
field_types.seq: int or null (null for a row the window made itself: a note, help, a sign-in card)
field_types.kind: string (kernel envelope kind, or local:note, local:help, local:auth for rows the window made)

tags.name: TRANSCRIPT_CHIPS_DRAWN
tags.note: A recorded message's row drew its chips (ADD-TO-MESSAGE-2026-11-10-r3, what you see; D94): chips counts the message's attachments, by_reference those that went as their reference line, drawn with a dashed outline and the reason on hover. Written once per row, with the record's seq; the view pair of the server's TURN_ACCEPTED attachments and by_reference. No label or path (E1).

tags.name: TRANSCRIPT_ROW_SKIPPED
tags.note: A record entry the pane received and drew as no row of its own, with why. hidden_kind: the controller's KIND_DISPOSITION ignores the kind (bookkeeping such as TriggerFired, PromptFragment); folded: drawn inside another row (a tool result or tool progress inside its call's card); duplicate_seq: an entry the stream replayed, already held; other: a kind the controller renders that made no row this time (an empty model reply, a final answer repeating the reply, SessionStarted shown in the pane's header).
tags.emit_site: web/vm/session_controller.ts handleEnvelope (hidden_kind, duplicate_seq, other, tool progress folded); web/reveal/transcript/Transcript.tsx (tool results folded)

field_types.session_id: string or null (the kernel session id; null in a pane showing an attached record, whose RECORD_OPENED names it)

tags.name: WORKSPACE_ADDED
tags.note: A folder was sent to the recent-workspace list. outcome: added, refused.

tags.name: CONTROLS_PICKED
tags.note: The length and tone picks were recorded for the next session.

tags.name: SESSION_RENAMED
tags.note: A session's name changed. outcome: renamed, refused.

tags.name: TASK_STOP_REQUESTED
tags.note: The person asked a background task to stop.

tags.name: CLI_STATUS_CHECKED
tags.note: The window asked whether a CLI driver is signed in.

tags.name: CLI_LOGIN_PROMPTED
tags.note: The sign-in card was shown for a CLI driver.

tags.name: CLI_LOGIN_FINISHED
tags.note: The sign-in card's flow ended. outcome: signed_in, failed, dismissed.

tags.name: SERVER_STARTED
tags.note: The server bound its port; written before either listener serves, so it is the server's first record (S1) and opens server_run. The store's counts follow in STORE_SCANNED.
tags.emit_site: server.py main, after the port readback

tags.name: STORE_SCANNED
tags.note: The server's boot scan of the session store finished; the store as found. The scan runs on a background thread while the server serves, so request records may precede it.

field_types.sessions_found: int (session manifests the boot scan read)

tags.name: SESSION_CREATED
tags.note: The server created a session for a window's open request.

field_types.workspace_shape: enum flat | worktree | isolate (the kernel's WorkspaceShape)

tags.name: TURN_ACCEPTED
tags.note: The server accepted a turn and handed it to the kernel, with the number of attachments its UserMessage carries. v0.51: by_reference, the attachments that went as their reference line, not their content (a binary, missing, unreadable or image file, or one past the 64 KB a file or the 256 KB a message inlines; ADD-TO-MESSAGE-2026-11-10-r3).

field_types.attachments: int (count of the turn's attachments; kinds, refs and text are on the record's UserMessage)
field_types.by_reference: int (attachments sent as a reference line; sprint 446)

tags.name: API_REFUSED
tags.note: The server answered an /api/ request with an error (status 400 or over). area: the domain its path names, unrouted when no route serves the path; cause: the handler function and line that refused, never the request's content.
tags.emit_site: server.py Handler._send, for every /api/ response of status 400 or over

field_types.area: enum session | turn | workspace | files | records | cli | runs | tasks | assays | topology | models | bundles | language | children | mcp | agent | diff | unrouted
field_types.cause: string (the refusing handler and line, function:line in server.py; the response text stays in the window's *_REFUSED detail)

tags.name: SERVER_FAULTED
tags.note: An exception escaped a handler; the request failed with 500.

field_types.area: enum session | turn | workspace | files | records | cli | runs | tasks | assays | topology | models | bundles | language | children | mcp | agent | diff | unrouted

tags.name: SERVER_STOPPED
tags.note: The server's shutdown ended its sessions and exited.

tags.name: TRACE_OPENED
tags.note: A process opened its trace file for this launch.

tags.name: TRACE_LOST
tags.note: Lines that could not be written since the last line that was.

tags.name: SIGNAL_REJECTED
tags.note: An emit broke the vocabulary: an unknown tag, a required field missing, a field not declared, a value of the wrong type (field_types) or out of range (E5). Raised in source and test builds; written in the packaged app (E6), and the rejected record is not. Retired in v0.16: the code names tags, fields and values through types generated from this file (scripts/gen_signals.py), so the compiler rejects a broken emit and no runtime checker writes this record.

field_types.problem: enum unknown_tag | missing_field | extra_field | wrong_type | out_of_range
field_types.field: string (the payload field at fault; absent for unknown_tag)

tags.name: INVARIANT_BROKEN
tags.note: A Layer 4–5 rule failed at runtime; context holds the recent trace and the state involved.
tags.emit_site: electron/invariants.ts (the runtime checker), fed by electron/main.ts with every record main writes

field_types.rule: string (rule id in state_transitions, temporal_invariants or evidence_constraints)
field_types.context: object (recent records and the state the rule read)

tags.name: RECORD_OPENED
tags.note: A pane attached a run record read-only (attachRecordRoot). how: open_record (File ▸ Open Record or ⌘O), deep_link (a substrate://record/ link), run (a run pane showing its run's record). outcome: attached when the record's stream opens, refused when it errors or closes first.

tags.name: PANE_DRAWN
tags.note: A pane's drawn state changed: written from the commit, with the values App published to the areas that draw the pane, when any field differs from the pane's last record. state: picker (the pane shows its picker), session (it shows a session, or is bound and its session not yet opened), record (a run's record). A picker record carries picker_line, armed, folder_rows (rows in the workspace column: the sandbox, choose folder, recent and typed folders, not the sessions under an open row), model_rows (rows in the model column) and driver_shown. A session or record carries connection, turn_state (what the activity line draws: idle, no turn yet; running, a live turn; parked, the last turn returned or parked; ended, the session ended; failed, the last turn's request failed), driver_shown, named (the session has a name), and session_id when the pane holds one. The view pair of the picker, session-open, stream, turn, driver and workspace tags.

field_types.picker_line: enum ws | model | guidance | length | tone
field_types.connection: enum idle | connecting | connected | reconnecting | closed
field_types.turn_state: enum idle | running | parked | ended | failed

tags.name: PAGE_DRAWN
tags.note: A page committed its rows: records, assays, studio. inert is true for a page with no endpoint behind it (studio). The view pair of the *_LOADED tags.

tags.name: TRANSCRIPT_SCROLLED
tags.note: Where a pane's transcript sits after a change. at_bottom: within STICK_PX of the bottom; following: new content will scroll into view; pinned: a clicked card header is held in place, which overrides following until the user scrolls. cause: row_arrived (a React commit of the pane's rows), user (the user scrolled), resized (the layout changed outside a commit: a card opened or closed, the window resized), view_switch (the pane's transcript shown again, its saved place restored). Written for view_switch each time; for the other causes only when at_bottom, following or pinned differs from the last record for that pane and view. The first draw of a pane's transcript writes nothing.

tags.name: WINDOW_FAULTED
tags.note: An error escaped the window's code: an uncaught exception (a render error that no boundary catches reaches it too), an unhandled promise rejection, or a preload script that threw (written by main for that window). No message text (E1).

field_types.error_type: string (the error's class name, e.g. TypeError; non-error when what was thrown is not an Error)
field_types.where: string (script file name and line, e.g. index-abc.js:12; unknown when none is given)

tags.name: MAIN_FAULTED
tags.note: An error escaped Electron main: an uncaught exception (Electron then shows its error dialog) or an unhandled rejection (Electron prints a warning and goes on). Observed, never handled: the app behaves as without the record.

field_types.error_type: string (the error's class name; non-error when what was thrown is not an Error)

tags.name: RENDERER_GONE
tags.note: A window's renderer process ended (Electron render-process-gone); the window shows nothing until it is reloaded or closed.

field_types.reason: enum clean_exit | abnormal_exit | killed | crashed | oom | launch_failed | integrity_failure | memory_eviction

tags.name: WINDOW_UNRESPONSIVE
tags.note: A window's renderer stopped answering (Electron unresponsive). Written once per hang: Electron repeats the event about every 16 s while the renderer stays hung.

tags.name: WINDOW_RESPONSIVE
tags.note: A window that was unresponsive answers again (Electron responsive).

field_types.unresponsive_ms: int (since its WINDOW_UNRESPONSIVE, on main's clock)

tags.name: CHILD_PROCESS_GONE
tags.note: An Electron child process other than a renderer ended unexpectedly (Electron child-process-gone).

field_types.type: enum utility | zygote | sandbox_helper | gpu | pepper_plugin | pepper_plugin_broker | unknown
field_types.reason: enum clean_exit | abnormal_exit | killed | crashed | oom | launch_failed | integrity_failure | memory_eviction

tags.name: RUN_FAULTED
tags.note: A topology run in the background raised; the run's status poll reports the error.

field_types.run_id: string (the run's id, as RUN_STARTED names it)
field_types.where: string (the deepest server.py function the exception passed through)

tags.name: SERVER_UNCAUGHT
tags.note: An exception escaped a server thread outside the request handlers (threading.excepthook, sys.excepthook); Python then prints it as before.

field_types.where: string (the deepest server.py function the exception passed through)

tags.name: STREAM_DIRECTION_SET
tags.note: Meta's stream lens changed its direction. Written when it differs from the one shown.

tags.name: STREAM_LEVEL_SET
tags.note: Meta's stream lens changed its level: every event, or the machinery hidden. Written when it differs.

tags.name: SEQ_SELECTED
tags.note: Meta lit a record seq to inspect, or cleared it. Written when the lit seq changes. editor_activity (v0.38): ACTIVITY's ◂ in the editor's inspector opened the meta pane inside the editor on that seq.

field_types.seq: int or null (the record seq lit; null when the click cleared it)
field_types.how: enum stream_row | side_graph | language_row | language_key | language_open | editor_activity

tags.name: LANGUAGE_STREAM_SET
tags.note: The language lens changed the stream it reads. Written when it differs.

tags.name: LANGUAGE_VIEW_SET
tags.note: The language lens changed its view (sides is the side by side view). Written when it differs.

field_types.view: enum bars | deviation | ribbons | sides | measures

tags.name: LANGUAGE_LANE_SET
tags.note: The language lens moved its focus to another lane. Written when it differs.

tags.name: FIND_OPENED
tags.note: The find bar opened (⌘F).

tags.name: FIND_CLOSED
tags.note: The find bar closed: ⌘F again, or Escape.

tags.name: FIND_QUERY_CHANGED
tags.note: The find query changed.

field_types.length: int (characters in the query; never the query, E1)

tags.name: FIND_SCOPE_SET
tags.note: Find's scope moved to the lens last clicked. Written when it differs.

tags.name: TOP_BAR_CARD_SET
tags.note: A top bar card opened or closed in its pane's state: its chip clicked, Escape, a click outside the cards, a model picked in a pane's picker (⌘D focuses a new pane's picker and leaves the card's pane holding it open), or the other card opened. A card hidden because another pane took the focus is still open and writes nothing.

field_types.cause: enum click | escape | outside | picked | other_card

tags.name: TOOL_CARD_TOGGLED
tags.note: A click opened or closed one tool card. A card opened or closed by the fold toggle writes nothing; TOOL_OUTPUT_MODE_SET names that.

field_types.seq: int or null (the ToolCall row's seq)

tags.name: TOOL_OUTPUT_MODE_SET
tags.note: Every tool card's output was folded or unfolded: ⌘E, /fold or /unfold. Written each time it is applied: a second /unfold reopens the cards a click closed.

tags.name: FILES_LISTED
tags.note: The workspace file API listed a folder of the session's workspace. The folder's path stays out of the trace (E1).

tags.name: FILE_READ
tags.note: The workspace file API read one file's facts, and its text when it is UTF-8 under the cap. No path or text in the trace (E1). v0.61: a text file in another encoding is read and named (utf8_bom, utf16, latin1), by the attachments' decoding rule (a byte-order mark, else a NUL byte in the first 8 KB is binary, else UTF-8, else Latin-1); the editor opens it read-only.

field_types.encoding: enum utf8 | utf8_bom | utf16 | latin1 | binary | too_large

tags.name: FILE_BYTES_READ
tags.note: A slice of a file read for the editor's bytes view (sprint 463; roadmap r13 E14): GET /api/session/<id>/bytes, at most 256 KB from `offset`. Every file that is not text, at any size, is read this way as the person scrolls. No path or byte in the payload (E1).

tags.name: FILE_LINES_READ
tags.note: A range of a text file's lines read for the editor's lines view (sprint 469; roadmap r13 E14): GET /api/session/<id>/lines, at most 2,000 lines from `from`, a line past 64 KB sent in part. A text file over the read limit is read this way as the person scrolls, after one pass that indexes its lines. No path or text in the payload (E1).

tags.name: FILE_WRITTEN
tags.note: A view saved a file in the session's workspace, and the kernel record holds the edit as FileWritten (SessionRegistry.append_event). A write the record refuses leaves the file untouched and is an API_REFUSED. v0.36: off_record — the session's record could not take the edit (an ended session, or no record yet) and the file was written all the same: the editor is an editor whether the session is on or off (the Architect, 2026-11-09). v0.63 (sprint 465): encoding, how the text was written: utf8; utf8_bom and utf16 keep the file's mark and byte order; latin1 for a Latin-1 text file; bytes for a file that is not text, its text every byte one character, written byte for byte. `bytes` counts the bytes written.

field_types.bytes: int (the new text's size in UTF-8)
field_types.created: bool (the file did not exist before)
field_types.seq: int or null (the FileWritten entry's seq on the kernel record; null for live, whose seq the turn's writer assigns, and for off_record)
field_types.encoding: enum utf8 | utf8_bom | utf16 | latin1 | bytes

tags.name: FILES_WATCH_OPENED
tags.note: A client opened the workspace watch stream.

tags.name: FILES_WATCH_CLOSED
tags.note: The workspace watch stream ended: the client hung up.

field_types.change_events: int (change events sent on the stream)

tags.name: EDITOR_OPENED
tags.note: The code editor view opened in a pane (⌘⇧E). binding is the active keybinding mode. Opens an editor_run session. binding is optional from v0.29: written once the binding setting exists (Phase 2). v0.33: binding required (the setting exists, sprint 423). v0.36: binding standard, the default (a normal editor; vim and nano are options, the Architect 2026-11-09).

tags.name: EDITOR_CLOSED
tags.note: The code editor view closed, returning to the pane's terminal or meta view. tab_count is the number of open file tabs at close. Closes the editor_run session.

tags.name: EDITOR_FILE_OPENED
tags.note: A file opened in the editor's tab row. how names the source of the open. tab_count is the number of open tabs after the open. The file is identified by following the pane's session_id and the seq of the FILE_READ that loaded it (E1: no path in the trace). v0.46: activity (a click in the left column's activity tab); open_tab (the open tab, which lists only files already open, so it shows a tab and writes none today).

field_types.how: enum tree | quick_open | follow | search | deep_link | open_tab | activity

tags.name: EDITOR_FILE_SHOWN
tags.note: The centre placed a different file's text (sprint 473; BLACKBOARD 2026-11-11, the editor broken in use): ms from its read being asked to the text placed, once per file shown (an open, a tab switch, a kept buffer placed). The base comparison applies after it and is not counted. A performance timeline (foundation 01): the trace and the gates measure the time to show a file. No path or text in the payload (E1).

field_types.ms: int (milliseconds from the read asked to the text placed)

tags.name: EDITOR_FILE_SAVED
tags.note: A file saved from the editor. command names which keybinding or menu item triggered the save. Pairs with a FILE_WRITTEN on the server.

tags.name: EDITOR_SAVE_CONFLICTED
tags.note: A save from the editor was refused because the file changed on disk since the buffer read it (the server's 409, an API_REFUSED area files status 409); the editor keeps the buffer and draws the offer to reload the file or overwrite it (roadmap r8 E4). Pairs with EDITOR_DRAWN.conflict true.

tags.name: EDITOR_CONFLICT_RESOLVED
tags.note: The reload-or-overwrite offer was answered. reload: the buffer is dropped and the file read again from disk; overwrite: the buffer is saved over the file (an EDITOR_FILE_SAVED and FILE_WRITTEN follow). Pairs with EDITOR_DRAWN.conflict false.

tags.name: EDITOR_FILE_CLOSED
tags.note: A tab closed in the editor. tab_count is the remaining open tabs.

tags.name: EDITOR_COLUMN_FOLDED
tags.note: A column folded to its labelled rail or unfolded. column names which of the three panels. cause (v0.29): key (⌥⌘L, ⌥⌘R, ⌘J), menu (View), rail (a click on the rail's ◂ or ▸, or the column header's), focus (View ▸ Focus folding or restoring it).

tags.name: EDITOR_FOLLOW_MARKED
tags.note: The editor, open in the pane, marked a session edit at its call (roadmap r10 E7; D93): a ToolCall to edit_file or write_file on a file of the session's workspace. seq is the call's seq on the session record. On the file shown, the lines the call replaces are marked and scrolled into view; on another file, its row in the tree is marked; the view stays (the person's focus wins). Resolved by one EDITOR_FOLLOW_CONFIRMED or EDITOR_FOLLOW_WITHDRAWN with the same seq (S10).

field_types.seq: int (sequence number of the ToolCall or HarnessToolCall on the session record)

tags.name: EDITOR_FOLLOW_CONFIRMED
tags.note: The followed edit's result arrived ok: the file is read again; on the file shown, its first changed line is brought into view. v0.40: seq is the call's (it was the result's, which left S10 unpairable); result_seq added.

field_types.conflict: bool (the buffer of the file had unsaved changes: it is kept, and the next save is refused as stale and offers reload or overwrite)

tags.name: EDITOR_FOLLOW_WITHDRAWN
tags.note: The followed edit failed (its ToolResult ok false): the mark is removed and the file is unchanged. v0.40: seq is the call's; result_seq added.

tags.name: EDITOR_HUNK_DRAWN
tags.note: A diff hunk rendered in the inspector's 'changes in this file' section. author is attributed by walking the unified HISTORY list in reverse; the first entry whose written range overlaps the hunk is the author. View-category tag: the view-side counterpart of the diff computation.

tags.name: EDITOR_BYTES_VIEWED
tags.note: The editor showed a file that is not text as its bytes (sprint 463; roadmap r13 E14), in one of four forms: hex (hexdump -C), binary (xxd -b), octal (od -b), text (the bytes as Latin-1). how: open (the file opened in the view) or selector (the form picked in the status line). bytes: the file's size.

tags.name: EDITOR_CHIP_ADDED
tags.note: A file, folder, or line range added to the input bar as an attachment chip (⌥-click, drag, or right-click › Add to message). v0.49: emitted (sprint 443) for ⌥-click on a file or folder in the editor's tree; range follows with the editor's line sources. v0.57: how, the gesture: alt_click (⌥-click in the tree) or key (⌥A in the code since v0.58, ⌘⇧A in v0.57: the selection as a range, or the file with nothing selected). v0.59: how menu, right-click › Add to message on a tree row, a tab, a search result or the code. v0.60: how drag, a tree row, a tab or a search result dropped on the input bar.

tags.name: EDITOR_SAVED_FOR_SEND
tags.note: A turn was about to be posted from a pane whose session had buffers differing from their files as read; each was saved through the file API with FileWritten view send before the turn (the Architect, 2026-11-10: what is on screen is what the model sees). files counts the saves written, refused the saves refused as stale (409), which leave the file unwritten and a warning row under the message. Precedes the pane's TURN_SUBMITTED for that turn, whose saved equals files. Not written when there was nothing to save. No paths in the trace (E1).

tags.name: INPUT_CHIP_REMOVED
tags.note: A chip removed from the input bar before sending: its × (how x) or ⌫ at the start of an empty draft (how backspace; D94). No label or path in the trace (E1).

tags.name: INPUT_DRAFT_RESTORED
tags.note: A message the server refused (TURN_REFUSED) went back into its pane's input bar: its line and its chips, so nothing is lost (ADD-TO-MESSAGE-2026-11-10-r3: a real error leaves the draft and its chips in the bar). Written only when the bar was still empty; anything typed since is kept. chips counts the chips put back. No text or path in the trace (E1).

tags.name: EDITOR_TREE_FOUND
tags.note: The tree's find (⌥⌘F with the tree focused, VS Code's Explorer find) drew a result: filter shows only the matches and their folders, unopened ones included; highlight lights the matches in the tree and badges each collapsed folder holding some. The name stays out of the trace (E1). Pairs with FILES_FOUND and EDITOR_DRAWN.tree_rows.

tags.name: EDITOR_SEARCH_QUERIED
tags.note: A workspace search dispatched (⌘⇧F). result_file_count is the number of files with matches; result_match_count is the total match count. The query text stays out of the trace (E1). v0.41: each dispatch pairs with one FILES_SEARCHED; result_match_count counts the matches in the returned lines. v0.42: word (whole word); result_match_count is the server's match count. v0.48: name_count, the names section's rows.

field_types.name_count: int (files and folders listed by name)

tags.name: EDITOR_SEARCH_REPLACED
tags.note: A replace from the left column's search: every match (⌘⇧↵ or all), the matches in one file, or one match. files counts the files written through the file API; count the matches replaced; refused the files whose write was refused as stale (409). The search runs again after it. No texts or paths in the trace (E1). v0.43: a file with unsaved edits is replaced in its buffer, then saved (buffers).

field_types.buffers: int (files replaced in their unsaved buffer and saved from it)

tags.name: EDITOR_SEARCH_REPLACE_UNDONE
tags.note: The last replace from the left column's search undone in one step: every file it changed written back to its text before the replace, through the file API (a buffer through its own save). files counts the files written back; refused those changed since the replace (409), left as they are. No texts or paths in the trace (E1).

tags.name: EDITOR_FIND_QUERIED
tags.note: A find in the open file (the inspector's FIND / REPLACE; ⌘F in the editor): the query settled (a pause in typing, or Aa or .* switched) and the buffer's matches were counted and marked. The query text stays out of the trace (E1). Pairs with the count the section draws. v0.45: whole_word, in_selection.

field_types.match_count: int (matches in the open file's buffer)
field_types.in_selection: bool (held to the range taken from the selection)

tags.name: EDITOR_REPLACED
tags.note: A replace in the open file's buffer from FIND / REPLACE: one (↵) or all. The buffer changes and stays unsaved until a save; the texts stay out of the trace (E1). v0.45: preserve_case.

field_types.preserve_case: bool (each replacement in its match's case, VS Code's rule)

tags.name: EDITOR_QUICK_OPENED
tags.note: The quick-open overlay opened (⌘P). The selection, if any, fires as EDITOR_FILE_OPENED with how=quick_open. v0.47: emitted (sprint 441): ⌘P in the editor or Go ▸ Quick Open.

tags.name: EDITOR_INSPECTOR_SWAPPED
tags.note: ⌘M (or View ▸ Meta) in the editor opened the meta pane inside the editor view, in the right column in place of the inspector (showing lenses), or closed it (showing spine); the editor stays the view (no VIEW_CHANGED). The Architect, 2026-11-09: "It's command M. It's the meta pane"; no chip. Emitted from sprint 430; the meta pane is 400 px, the inspector its column's width.

tags.name: EDITOR_KEY_REFUSED
tags.note: A key binding refused in context. key is the named key combo (never a typed character). reason classifies why the action could not proceed. Diagnostic-required per E9. no_session (v0.29): ⌘⇧E or View ▸ Editor while the focused pane is at its picker with no session. no_split (v0.30): ⌘D or ⌘⇧D in the editor, which does not split (D49 (c), spec r6 §4). not_editor and no_file (v0.34): ⌘S outside the editor; ⌘S or ⌘W in the editor with no file open (roadmap r8, the key table). not_utf8 (v0.61): ⌘S on a file opened read-only because its encoding is not plain UTF-8. not_utf8 is no longer written from v0.63: every file saves in its own encoding (sprint 465).

field_types.key: string (named key with modifiers, as KEY_ROUTED)
field_types.reason: enum no_session | no_split | ended_session | view_only | binary_file | over_cap | no_git | not_editor | no_file | not_utf8

tags.name: EDITOR_DRAWN
tags.note: The editor view rendered its structural state. The view-category tag for the editor: pairs with EDITOR_OPENED, EDITOR_FILE_OPENED, EDITOR_COLUMN_FOLDED, EDITOR_FOLLOW_MARKED, EDITOR_CHIP_ADDED, EDITOR_SEARCH_QUERIED, EDITOR_INSPECTOR_SWAPPED, and the column/tab changes. Written from the commit when any field differs from the editor's last record. v0.29: dock, sides_swapped and focus draw R7–R9; tree_rows pairs with FILES_LISTED, modified_dots with DIFF_READ. v0.32: the inspector's drawn counts (spec r6 §5.0; frame 24a), 0 with no file open. v0.33: binding required; mode, read_only and unsaved draw the status line and the buffer's state (sprint 424); the anchor's third row carries them. v0.34: conflict; the anchor's third row carries it (magic 0xB7). v0.36: binding standard, the default (a normal editor; vim and nano are options, the Architect 2026-11-09). read_only removed (v0.36): no file is read-only. v0.38: showing follows the right column (spine: the inspector; lenses: the meta pane open in the editor, ⌘M); the anchor's third row carries it (magic 0xB9). v0.40: follow_marks; the anchor's third row carries it (magic 0xBA). v0.41: left_tab follows the left column's tab (files or search; open and activity when drawn); the anchor's third row carries it.

field_types.showing: enum spine | lenses (inspector or record lenses)
field_types.tree_rows: int (rows the files tree draws: entries of every open folder)
field_types.modified_dots: int (files the tree draws with the changed-vs-main dot)
field_types.hunks: int (hunks CHANGES IN THIS FILE draws)
field_types.activity_rows: int (ACTIVITY rows: this file's calls on the record)
field_types.history_rows: int (HISTORY rows: the file's edits, by the session and by hand)
field_types.mode: enum normal | insert | visual | replace | none (the vim mode the status line shows; none under nano or with no file open)
field_types.unsaved: int (open files whose buffers differ from the file as read)
field_types.conflict: bool (the shown file's save was refused as stale and the reload-or-overwrite offer is drawn)
field_types.follow_marks: int (session edits marked and not yet resolved: EDITOR_FOLLOW_MARKED without its CONFIRMED or WITHDRAWN)

tags.name: EDITOR_DOCK_SET
tags.note: The editor's substrate terminal docked below the centre (bottom, the default) or as a column beside it (right), from View ▸ Dock Terminal (spec r6 §5.1 (2)).

tags.name: EDITOR_SIDES_SWAPPED
tags.note: The editor's side columns swapped places (true: files right, inspector left) or swapped back, from View ▸ Swap Sides (spec r6 §5.1 (3)).

tags.name: EDITOR_FOCUS_SET
tags.note: Focus turned on (both side columns to rails, the bottom panel to its sill; the prompt stays) or off (the layout before it restored), from View ▸ Focus (spec r6 §5.1 (4); frame 16c). Each column it folds or unfolds writes EDITOR_COLUMN_FOLDED with cause focus.

tags.name: EDITOR_COLUMN_RESIZED
tags.note: A divider drag ended and the column's size is remembered for the mode (spec r6 §5.1 (5)). Written once per drag, at its end. v0.52: ended, how the drag ended: pointerup (the button released over the captured handle); cancelled (the browser sent pointercancel); blurred (the capture ended with the window out of focus); capture_lost (the capture ended otherwise). Without a pointerup the drag stops where it was.

field_types.size: int (CSS px at the drag's end: a side column's width; the bottom panel's height, or its width when docked right)

tags.name: DIFF_READ
tags.note: The server read the session workspace's changes against main's merge-base (the default branch when there is no main; HEAD, the last commit, when there is neither; no_commit in a repository with no commit, and none outside a git repository, both with files 0). Paths stay out of the trace (E1). v0.31: `?path=` reads one file's hunks; hunks is their count and files is 1 when the file has changes, else 0. v0.54: head and no_commit; first_commit retired (no longer written: a base of the first commit, or of git's empty tree for a repository with no commit, marked every later line added and drew the editor's text teal).

field_types.base: enum main | default_branch | head | no_commit | none
field_types.files: int (files changed vs the base, new files included)
field_types.hunks: int (hunks in the one file read with ?path=; absent on the whole-workspace read)

tags.name: FILES_LISTED_ALL
tags.note: The server listed every file of the session's workspace for quick open (GET …/files/list), from the search's own walk: ignore files applied in or out of a git repository, VS Code's skipped names and folders, symlinks not followed. No path in the trace (E1). truncated when the walk stopped at its file cap; unreadable counts folders it could not read.

tags.name: FILES_FOUND
tags.note: The server found the workspace's files and folders by name for the tree's find (GET …/files/find), from the search's own walk (ignored files are not found), case ignored; fuzzy reads abc as *a*b*c*. files at most 512; truncated when more matched or the walk was cut. No name or path in the trace (E1). v0.45: unreadable. v0.45: name_length.

field_types.unreadable: int (folders the walk could not read and skipped)
field_types.name_length: int (characters in the name the server was asked for; the name itself stays out, E1)

tags.name: FILES_SEARCHED
tags.note: The server searched the session's workspace with its own walk and Python's re (sprint 435; no git): VS Code's skipped names and folders, each folder's .gitignore and .ignore applied in or out of a git repository, hidden files searched, symlinks not followed, files over the read cap, binary or not UTF-8 skipped. The query, globs and paths stay out of the trace (E1). files counts the files with a match; lines the matching lines returned; matches the matches in them; truncated marks a result cut at the line cap or a walk cut at the file cap. A query or glob that does not compile is an API_REFUSED (area files). v0.42: the walk replaces git grep; word and matches added. v0.43: buffers. v0.45: unreadable. v0.48: the search bar matches names and paths too (SEARCH-BAR-2026-11-10); names counts them.

field_types.regex: bool (the query read as an extended regular expression; else a fixed string)
field_types.buffers: int (walked files read from the editor's unsaved text, not the disk)
field_types.unreadable: int (folders the walk could not read and skipped)
field_types.names: int (files and folders whose name or path matched)

tags.name: FILES_REPLACE_PREPARED
tags.note: The server worked out a workspace replace (POST …/search/replace): the new text of each file it changes and the hash each was read at, written nowhere. The page writes each file through PUT …/file (FILE_WRITTEN each). scope: every match the search finds, the matches in one file, or one match. No query, replacement or path in the trace (E1).

entities.name: AppBoot
entities.definition: One launch of the packaged or source app: Electron main starts, spawns the server, opens windows; ends at quit.

entities.name: Window
entities.definition: One BrowserWindow and its renderer; holds panes, the open view and pages.

entities.name: Server
entities.definition: The backend process server.py for one AppBoot: its port, its session registry.

entities.name: Pane
entities.definition: One cell of a window's grid; unbound (shows the picker) or bound to one session or record.

entities.name: Picker
entities.definition: A pane's workspace bar while unbound: the folder column and the model, guidance, length and tone lines; its armed folder.

entities.name: OpenView
entities.definition: Which view a window shows: panes, meta, or a page over one of them.

entities.name: Page
entities.definition: A full-window surface: records, assays, studio, settings.

entities.name: Lens
entities.definition: One way meta shows a session: stream, graph, structure, language, scene, i/o.

entities.name: Dialog
entities.definition: A modal the window opens (settings, end session, export, confirmations).

entities.name: KeyAction
entities.definition: What a key press did at window level, chosen by the key map.

entities.name: Stream
entities.definition: A pane's live connection to one session's record events (SSE), with its reconnects.

entities.name: Transcript
entities.definition: The rows a pane draws for a session, one per record event it shows.

entities.name: Workspace
entities.definition: The folder a session works in; the app keeps a recents list of them.

entities.name: Driver
entities.definition: The model or CLI agent a session runs on, with its version.

entities.name: Session
entities.definition: A kernel session: a manifest and a run record under ~/.substrate/sessions/<id>/.

entities.name: Turn
entities.definition: One user message and its reply within a session.

entities.name: RecordEntry
entities.definition: One envelope of a session's run record (kernel Envelope).

entities.name: Run
entities.definition: A topology run a session started or the user started.

entities.name: Task
entities.definition: A background command a session started.

entities.name: Child
entities.definition: A delegate session started by another session.

entities.name: Record
entities.definition: A run record opened read-only from the records page or a deep link.

entities.name: Spec
entities.definition: A topology spec authored in Studio.

entities.name: Assay
entities.definition: A test run's report shown on the assays page.

entities.name: CliLogin
entities.definition: A CLI driver's sign-in state and the card that asks for it.

entities.name: TraceFile
entities.definition: The on-disk trace a process writes for one AppBoot (plan item 2).

entities.name: EditorView
entities.definition: The code editor view in a pane, opened by ⌘⇧E: file tree, tab row, CodeMirror instances (held in the widget registry), inspector spine, column layout, quick open, and workspace search.
entities.source: design spec section 24; ROADMAP-2026-11-09-code-editor-r4.md; web/app/editor/ (the module, per canonical home)

record_context._comment: Layer 2 universal fields the emitter stamps on every trace record, outside the payload (PAYLOAD_FIELD_PROPOSED P-0.7-CONTEXT). They join every tag to its launch, process, order, window and pane.
record_context.boot_id: string: the AppBoot id main mints and passes to the window and the server
record_context.proc_seq: int: this process's record number within the boot, from 0; the order key
record_context.wall: string: ISO-8601 time written; recorded, never used to order
record_context.window_id: int or null: the BrowserWindow id (main and window records)
record_context.pane_id: int or null: the pane the record is about (a controller's own pane; the pane a window component draws or changes); null for window- or app-level records

sessions._comment: Layer 3. Nesting: app_boot contains server_run and window; window contains pane; pane contains picker_run and pane_session.

strata.name: window
strata.close: WINDOW_CLOSED (main's record; the window's own trace ends without a close tag when the window is destroyed)

strata.name: picker_run
strata.re_entry: PICKER_FOLDER_DISARMED returns to the folder column

strata.name: pane_session
strata.frames: session, turn, stream and transcript tags of the pane; joins the kernel Session by session_id

strata.name: editor_run
strata.note: v0.29: the editor is a window view on the focused pane's session; one editor_run at a time per window, under that pane. binding moved to optional.

invariants.ends_at: SERVER_EXITED: a server that exits binds and starts nothing, and SERVER_EXITED (expected false) is its incident
SERVER_EXITED: a server that exits binds and starts nothing, and SERVER_EXITED (expected false) is its incident

invariants.source: Nielsen, Usability Engineering (1993) ch. 5: 1.0 s is the limit for the user's flow of thought; the screen must show what the record holds within it
Nielsen 1993: 10 s is the limit for keeping attention on the dialogue

rules.statement: APP_BOOTED is main's first record of a boot; WINDOW_BOOTED a window's first; SERVER_STARTED the server's first, written when its port is bound and before it serves, unless the server dies before it binds, when its first record is the SERVER_UNCAUGHT it dies of.

APP_QUIT_COMPLETED is main's last record of a boot. A boot whose main.jsonl does not end with it ended without closing (killed or crashed); the next boot in the same trace folder finds it and writes INVARIANT_BROKEN S2 naming that boot and its last record (one app runs per machine, so the earlier boot has ended).
PICKER_FOLDER_ARMED precedes any PICKER_LINE_ENTERED of the same pane since its last PANE_OPENED or PICKER_FOLDER_DISARMED.
PICKER_COMMITTED follows PICKER_LINE_ENTERED with line tone for the same pane, and is followed by PANE_BOUND with how picker.

A pane holds one session at a time: its last SESSION_OPEN_ACKED or SESSION_ATTACH_STARTED names that session, replacing any before it, until PANE_CLOSED; every later TRANSCRIPT_ROW_DRAWN and TRANSCRIPT_ROW_SKIPPED of the pane that names a session names that one.
SESSION_OPEN_ACKED follows SESSION_OPEN_REQUESTED for the same pane.

Across processes: each SESSION_OPEN_ACKED (window) pairs with exactly one SESSION_CREATED (server) with the same session_id in the same boot, written before it. The server also creates sessions for other clients (its mcp and agent routes, a plain POST /api/session), which no window acks.

TURN_SUBMITTED for a pane names the session of that pane's last SESSION_OPEN_ACKED or SESSION_ATTACH_STARTED; across processes, a session's TURN_ACK records (window) never outnumber its TURN_ACCEPTED records (server) in the same boot, each written before the window's ack.
Each window *_REFUSED tag caused by a server answer pairs with one API_REFUSED (server) in the same boot.

EDITOR_FOLLOW_MARKED precedes exactly one EDITOR_FOLLOW_CONFIRMED or EDITOR_FOLLOW_WITHDRAWN for the same pane and seq (the call's seq, v0.40). A mark open when the pane's editor run ends (EDITOR_CLOSED, PANE_CLOSED, a reload) is dropped with the run: no editor record follows a run's end (S11). Checked in electron/invariants.ts from sprint 431.

operators.name: AppMain
operators.responsibilities: Launch, the server process, windows, native dialogs, menus, deep links; writes main's trace.

operators.name: WindowShell
operators.responsibilities: The window's open view, panes, focus, keys, dialogs and the picker.

operators.name: PaneController
operators.home: web/vm/session_controller.ts (one per pane, spawned by web/vm/pane_registry.ts)
operators.responsibilities: A pane's session: open, attach, turns, slash commands, stream, controls, CLI status.

operators.name: TranscriptRenderer
operators.responsibilities: Draws a pane's record entries as rows.

operators.name: Server
operators.responsibilities: HTTP API over the kernel: creates sessions, takes turns, serves records, files and rosters; resolves the driver a session runs on.
runtime_notes: route: driver resolved to a CLI agent, an Ollama model or deterministic; SESSION_CREATED.driver names it

operators.name: Sink
operators.home: the trace writers of main, the window and the server (plan item 2)
operators.responsibilities: Writes each process's records; counts what it could not write.

operators.name: EditorController
operators.responsibilities: The editor view's file tree, tab row, editor instances (via the widget registry), inspector spine with outline/changes/find/activity/history/info, columns, workspace search, quick open, follow marks, chips, and the diff vs main.
runtime_notes: EditorView is an entity (Layer 0) and, through its EditorController, an operator; same dual classification as Pane and Server

operators.dual_classification: Pane is an entity (Layer 0) and, through its PaneController, an operator; Server likewise. EditorView is an entity and, through its EditorController, an operator.

constraints.rule: No message text, model output, file contents, prompt text, environment values or credentials in any payload; such content lives in the kernel record, reached by session_id and seq.
constraints.enforceability: mechanical (the emitter refuses fields named text, content, prompt, output, token, password, key_value; the linter checks payload field names)

constraints.rule: SERVER_EXITED carries code and signal; NAVIGATION_BLOCKED target_kind; API_REFUSED area, status, cause; SERVER_FAULTED error_type and where; TRACE_LOST count; SIGNAL_REJECTED tag, problem, call_site; INVARIANT_BROKEN rule and context; FILE_SKIPPED-style refusals their reason.
APP_QUIT_COMPLETED, STORE_SCANNED, SERVER_STOPPED, PICKER_COMMITTED carry their outcome counts or binding.
A session_id names a session under the boot's store; a seq names an entry of that session's record.
constraints.enforceability: mechanical (the reader joins and reports what does not resolve)

constraints.rule: following and not pinned implies at_bottom: a transcript that says it follows the bottom is at the bottom.
constraints.enforceability: mechanical (harness/shakeout/transcript_follow.ts reads every record; the runtime checker of plan item 5)

constraints.rule: EDITOR_KEY_REFUSED carries key (the named key combo) and reason (the classified cause: ended_session, view_only, binary_file, over_cap, no_git).

report_binding.observed: every behaviour tag, merged across main, window and server by boot_id, proc_seq and the causal keys
report_binding.grammar_drift: SIGNAL_REJECTED, and the open proposals in ../proposals.json
